what_its_for: Disulfiram is used to help people with chronic alcoholism stop drinking alcohol. It works by causing very unpleasant reactions when you drink alcohol, which helps discourage drinking. It is used as part of a complete treatment program that also includes counseling and support.
how_to_take: Take disulfiram by mouth, usually once a day. You can take it with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Do NOT take this medicine if you have had any alcohol in the last 12 hours. Even small amounts of alcohol found in foods, sauces, cough syrups, mouthwash, or cologne can cause a bad reaction.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 500 mg (one tablet) taken once a day for the first 1 to 2 weeks. Your doctor may then lower your dose to a maintenance dose of 250 mg once daily. Your doctor will decide the right dose for you. Never take more than your doctor prescribes.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if you have NOT had any alcohol that day. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store disulfiram at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine after the expiration date on the label.
what_to_avoid: AVOID ALL FORMS OF ALCOHOL while taking disulfiram. This includes beer, wine, liquor, and products that contain alcohol such as mouthwash, cough and cold medicines, cooking wines, vinegars, sauces, and even some hand sanitizers or perfumes that you could accidentally inhale. Drinking alcohol while taking this medicine can cause a serious reaction within 10 minutes, including flushing, sweating, headache, nausea, vomiting, chest pain, fast heartbeat, dizziness, and low blood pressure. Reactions can be severe and even life-threatening. Also avoid metronidazole (Flagyl) and paraldehyde. Tell all your doctors and pharmacists you are taking disulfiram before starting any new medicine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you have a reaction to alcohol while on this medicine (flushing, chest pain, trouble breathing, fast heartbeat, severe vomiting, or fainting). Also call your doctor if you notice yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice), dark urine, severe stomach pain, unusual tiredness, skin rash, numbness or tingling in your hands or feet, vision changes, mood changes, confusion, or signs of depression or thoughts of harming yourself.
when_it_works: Disulfiram starts working within 1 to 2 hours after you take your first dose. Its effects can last for up to 2 weeks after you stop taking it, so you must continue to avoid all alcohol during that time. The medicine does not cure alcoholism on its own — it works best when combined with counseling and a support program.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The safety of this medicine during pregnancy and breastfeeding is not well established. Older adults: Use with caution; older adults may be more sensitive to side effects. Liver disease: Tell your doctor if you have liver problems, as this medicine can affect liver function. Kidney disease: Use with caution if you have kidney problems. Children: This medicine is generally not recommended for use in children.
